meaning: Training a pretrained checkpoint, or a small policy from random weights, on tens of episodes of one task on one arm; a one-GPU job of minutes to hours.
The labs' word for any training that starts from a pretrained checkpoint; in this dive, one-node post-training is the eight-GPU version of it.
The first training of a model, on data from many robots or on video, before it has seen the reader's robot; done by labs across many servers.
Further training that updates every weight of the model, so the GPU holds gradient and optimiser state for all of them.
A fine-tune that trains small matrices added beside the existing weights and leaves the base weights frozen, used when a full update does not fit in GPU memory.
A training setting where the vision-language model that reads images and the instruction is not updated and only the action head and a small layer feeding it train.
The number of GPUs a job holds multiplied by the hours it holds them; a measure of occupied GPU time that does not account for the GPU model.
A robot policy built from a vision-language backbone with an action head attached.
A model that predicts the latent representation of what comes next instead of its pixels.
A small policy trained from scratch per task that outputs a chunk of future actions per call.
Training in which a policy improves from scored attempts, here in a simulator, instead of from demonstrations.
One recorded attempt at the task, from start to end.
The SageMaker service that starts instances for one training job and shuts them down when it ends.
A persistent training cluster that SageMaker manages, run with Kubernetes or Slurm.
AWS's managed Lustre, a file system that many processes read in parallel.
An EC2 booking of GPU instances for a set window.
A SageMaker reservation of GPU instances for a training job or HyperPod cluster, for 1 to 182 days.
The AWS network interface that lets training processes on different servers exchange data without passing through the operating system's network stack.
A SageMaker HyperPod feature that rebuilds a failed node's training state from healthy peers instead of restarting from a saved checkpoint.
